subject: Micro-patch deployment advisory — urgent runtime fix (short notice)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: urgent telemetry -> micro-patch proposal

Team —

We’ve identified a regression in the low-latency runtime path introduced in last night’s rollout that intermittently corrupts a small percent of telemetry batches and can cause tail-latency spikes when KV-cache hit rates are high. It’s isolated to a kernel selection path on A100s at particular sequence-length distributions.

Impact summary:
- Affects ~0.8% of in-flight requests for customers routed to the affected pool (observed in US-west pools between 00:30–03:00 UTC).
- Errors are transient and do not persist across restarts, but they cause a small number of customer-facing 5xxs and telemetry gaps.

Mitigation we validated: a targeted micro-patch that reverts the kernel switch in that code path and tightens a failing assertion flag. Patch is small (~12 LOC), low-risk, and we validated on staging with no perf regression. We can push a hot micro-deploy to affected nodes with a 30–45 minute short window; node restarts will be rolling and should not exceed 2m connection hiccups per node.

Requesting approvals to notify affected customers and proceed with the patch at 09:30 PT. Marissa — recommend we offer a brief post-incident summary and a small credit for impacted token windows. Jonas — ops sign-off on the rollback script and can you staff the 09:30 window?

Attachments: micro_patch_v1.0-notes.txt, rollback_helper.sh

Rishi
Senior Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example.com>
To: Sara Hwang <sara@cloudwave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Micro-patch deployment advisory — urgent runtime fix (short notice)

Hi Sara —

I’m Soojin on the Redwood account team. I wanted to alert you that our engineering team identified a very small set of requests that may have seen transient errors earlier this morning. We’ve traced the root cause to a recent kernel-selection change on certain GPU pools and plan to deploy a targeted micro-patch to mitigate immediately.

Planned window (short notice):
- Start: 2027-04-10 09:30 PT (16:30 UTC)
- Duration: rolling updates across affected nodes, expected 30–45 minutes total
- User impact: brief, per-node connection hiccups (sessions should auto-retry). We do not expect lost data; any in-progress requests may see a retryable 5xx.

What we’re doing:
- Apply a low-risk micro-patch that reverts the kernel switch and tightens a safety check.
- Rolling restarts to minimize blast radius; we will not touch unrelated pools.
- We’ll monitor your traffic and can route requests to unaffected pools temporarily if you prefer.

Action items / asks for CloudWave:
- No immediate action required for most integrations. If you have long-lived streaming connections, a short reconnect (automated by SDKs) may be needed.
- If you want us to route CloudWave traffic to an unaffected pool for the duration, reply and we’ll perform the switch.

We’ll provide a quick status update immediately post-deploy and a short postmortem within 48 hours. Marissa from account ops is on copy for any billing/credit questions.

Apologies for the short notice — we prioritized getting a validated fix first to avoid unnecessary disruption.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.example.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Sara Hwang <sara@cloudwave.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example.com>
Cc: CloudWave Platform Team <platform@cloudwave.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Micro-patch deployment advisory — urgent runtime fix (short notice)

Thanks, Soojin —

Appreciate the heads-up and the quick turnaround. A couple quick questions for our ops team:
- Do you have an expected number of requests that might surface 5xx during the window?
- Is there a recommended TTL for retries on our side, or should we rely on SDK defaults?

We’re seeing occasional reconnects on long-lived streams in staging; please route our production traffic to an unaffected pool if that eases the risk. If you can do that, let us know when the cutover completes.

—Sara
Head of Platform, CloudWave
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example.com>
To: Sara Hwang <sara@cloudwave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Micro-patch deployment advisory — urgent runtime fix (short notice)

Sara — thanks for the quick reply and the permission to route. Quick responses to your asks: 

- Expected error volume: based on telemetry, roughly 0.7–1.0% of in-flight requests in the affected pool could have returned transient 5xx during the window. Absolute request counts vary by customer load; for CloudWave traffic during the interval we estimate ~420 requests potentially impacted (based on recent 1h averages).
- Retry guidance: SDK defaults (exponential backoff with 3 attempts) are sufficient. If you have custom retry logic, a 5–10s initial backoff is fine. Avoid tight immediate retries.

Routing action taken: we temporarily routed CloudWave to a healthy pool at 09:28 PT prior to the start, and then applied the micro-patch to the affected nodes in a rolling fashion. The micro-patch completed at 10:10 PT. We continued monitoring for two hours; telemetry shows resolution of the corrupted-batch signal and tail-latency restored to baseline.

Next steps we’ll deliver:
- Short postmortem (within 48 hours) with root cause, timeline, and mitigation steps. Link: https://drive.redwood.example.com/notes/CW-71-micropatch
- The patch is included in tomorrow’s minor release; if you prefer we can schedule an additional maintenance window at your convenience to apply any customer-side safe-config tweaks.
- Marissa will follow up on a goodwill credit for the impacted request window; she’s on copy.

If you need logs or a scoped export for your incident review, we can provide a zipped bundle from the affected window (we’ve attached a small sample with redacted IDs).

Apologies again for the disruption — please let me or Marissa know if you want a phone call to walk through the postmortem.

Sincerely,
Soojin Lee
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
